document.outcome: Period of a mass–spring system; T ∝ √m

content.text: A block of mass 0.20 kg hangs from a light vertical spring and oscillates with a period of 0.60 s. The block is replaced by a block of mass 0.80 kg on the same spring.
What is the period of oscillation of the 0.80 kg block?
Assumes the period is independent of mass (confusion with the simple pendulum): 0.60 s
Forgets the square root (T ∝ m): 0.60 × 4 = 2.4 s
T = 2π√(m/k), so T ∝ √m. The mass increases by a factor of 4; the period increases by a factor of √4 = 2: 2 × 0.60 = 1.2 s.

document.outcome: a = −ω²x; relation between frequency and angular frequency

content.text: A buoy floating on the sea moves vertically with simple harmonic motion of frequency 0.50 Hz and amplitude 0.40 m.
What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the buoy when its displacement from the equilibrium position is 0.20 m?
Uses the amplitude instead of the displacement (the maximum acceleration): 3.14² × 0.40 = 3.9
Takes 0.50 to be the period: ω = 2π / 0.50 = 12.6 rad s⁻¹; 12.6² × 0.20 = 31.6 ≈ 32

document.outcome: Qualitative description of energy changes (timing of the kinetic–potential conversion)

content.text: A trolley attached to a horizontal spring oscillates on a frictionless track with simple harmonic motion of period
What is the shortest time between an instant when the kinetic energy of the trolley is a maximum and an instant when the elastic potential energy of the spring is a maximum?
Takes the time to go from one extreme to the other (this is the time between two successive maximum values of the potential energy)
Assumes the energy conversion has the same period as the displacement and that the conversion takes a full period
Assumes the period of the energy is twice the period of the motion (it is actually half)

Kinetic energy is greatest at the equilibrium position, and potential energy is greatest at the largest displacement. Moving from the equilibrium position to an extreme takes a quarter of a period: T/4.
A particle moves with simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.10 m. The maximum speed of the particle is 2.0 m s⁻¹.
What is the speed of the particle when its displacement from the equilibrium position is 0.060 m?
Assumes the speed decreases linearly with displacement: 2.0 × (1 − 0.60) = 0.80
Takes the speed to be directly proportional to displacement (confusion with acceleration): 2.0 × 0.60 = 1.2
